items.text: Pazi, da ne počiš, gospod Kurčon.
items.q: Hooman shortens his rude nickname for Eskandar to 'gospod Kurčon' as Eskandar puffs himself up. Does this jab sound natural?

items.text: Ja, kupil ti bom puncko. Ko dobim denar, ti kupim še boljšo, Babova punčka.
items.q: A stranger on the street answers his little girl, playfully copying her baby talk. Does that come through?
before: – Vžžž, Baba, Baba, mi kupis to veliko puncko?

items.text: Opravljanje? Opravljanje je, kadar ti niso storili nič slabega.
items.q: Maman, irritated, says talking about someone only counts as gossip if they haven't wronged you. Does 'Opravljanje' mean gossip here?
before: Maman obrne glavo v smer Mahboubehinega glasu in z rahlo razdraženim tonom reče:

items.text: Možganadrek. Siliš me, da vse povem do konca.
items.q: Hooman calls a roommate shit-for-brains. Does 'Možganadrek' work as a crude insult?
before: – Ja, no, glas se je razširil po fakulteti.

items.text: Ja, brž ko nas zagledajo, stisnejo ritne razpoke in se tako oddaljijo od nas, da bi jim najraje z obema nogama skočil v obraz.
items.q: Farid says the Tehran students clench their asses in disgust when they see them. Does 'stisnejo ritne razpoke' sound natural?

items.text: Stari, namesto da se tako vlečeš po postelji in se igraš z jajci, vstani in jih pošlji.
items.q: Hooman crudely tells lazy Amir to stop lolling on the bed and get on with it. Does this sound natural?

items.text: Če gre za leta, bi moral Bahmanu lizati jajca.
items.q: Hooman mocks a roommate who demands respect for his age. Does this crude retort sound natural?
before: Hooman je proti Eskandarju nameril svoj debeli, zaobljeni palec in rekel:

items.text: Odgovor je, da ti ne pristoji lizati riti mojstru Hoomanu.
items.q: Hooman crudely tells a roommate that kissing his ass doesn't suit him. Does this sound like dorm talk?
before: Eskandar ni hotel odnehati. Rekel je, da je treba to raziskati do korena, in bil je prepričan, da bi, če bi se našel odgovor na to vprašanje, to bila velika pomoč Hoomanu in vsemu človeštvu. Hooman je rekel:

items.text: Ti si večji vol od vseh. In postavo imaš za to.
items.q: A young man insults a heavy-set roommate as the biggest ox of all. Does this sound natural?
before: – Pojej mu glavo, no, nimamo živcev zate. Kaj ti veš, kaj pomeni elektrotehnika na Sharifu? In sploh, te je kdo vprašal za mnenje?

items.text: Leopard Farid, obvladaj živce in ne naredi morilske poteze.
items.q: Hooman jokingly warns hot-headed Farid not to pull one of his murderous stunts. Does 'morilske poteze' sound natural?

items.text: No, pojdi in kupi. Ko se steklo razbije, ne reci, da te nisem opozoril.
items.q: Hamid, a boy, loses his temper in an argument with a friend. Does it sound like a child arguing?
before: – Pfff, osel, kdo ve bolje – prijatelj bratranca mojstra našega svaka, ki je najbogatejši človek v Teheranu, ali ti, tele?

items.text: Rada bi, da bi postal odvisnik in ne bil takšen.
items.q: Maman says she would rather her husband were an addict than the way he is. Does it sound natural?

items.text: Tako me razjeziš, kadar tako molče sediš. Najraje bi te udarila s pestjo.
items.q: A girl, exasperated by his silence, says she wants to punch him. Does this sound natural?
before: …da angel ne ve ničesar o ljubezni in ljubljenju, zato je svoja razodetja lepote namenil Adamu. Kako potem pričakuješ, da bo Njegovo stvarjenje gorelo za nekoga, ki o ljubezni ne ve niti prve stvari? Vzdihnila je. Para njenega diha se je v zavojih dvigala proti nebu, jaz pa sem jo molče gledal.

items.text: »Tisto vino, ki je tam, je resnica ne prispodoba.«
items.q: Hafez's line, read one way: the wine is real, not a metaphor. Read another: not real, only a metaphor. Do both readings work here?
before: – To je. To poslušaj. Ti, za božjo voljo, poslušaj.

items.text: Ne vsak, ki povzroči, da njegov lastni obraz zažari, obvlada umetnost kradenja src; ne vsak, ki izdela ogledalo, pozna Aleksandrovo veščino.
items.q: He reads her a Hafez couplet about blushing and mirror-making. Does it read as poetry?
before: …namrščila, vrgla bo za teboj še par kletvic. Odprl sem knjigo. Izdihnila je zadržani dih iz prsi in rekla: – Spet hoče brati pesem. Resnično ne morem doumeti – tako majhna knjiga, in karkoli se zgodi, vedno v njej najdeš nekaj za to. Nič nisem rekel. – Prav, prav, ne kujaj se, beri. Bral sem: –
